messages:
anya: Heads-up: in a migration test we split a hot prefix across two nodes and saw tombstones vanish from the new owner, causing stale reads and duplicate apply attempts. Short log: 

```
[2026-02-14T09:04:21Z] split: prefix=acct7/pay epoch=201 demote_token=dt:77
[2026-02-14T09:04:21Z] compact: tombstones compaction -> removed 12 entries
[2026-02-14T09:04:22Z] handoff: new_owner accepted token=dt:77
[2026-02-14T09:04:23Z] read: key=acct7/pay:txn123 -> value=present (should be tombstoned)
```

ryan: Hmm. Did compaction run on the old owner before the handoff? If it dropped tombstones that hadn't propagated, new owner might never learn of them.

anya: Yep compaction triggered just before demote to reclaim space. Old owner removed tombstones that were only indexed locally.

marco: Are tombstones replicated to the shared index or only local markers? My understanding: we only log tombstone digests for large batches, not every tombstone.

emma: Correct. We have opportunistic tombstone propagation to the central index for GC, but it's not synchronous. That was to avoid write amplification.

ryan: That explains the correctness hole. If demote emits a token before tombstone propagation, new owner will see keys as live. Two paths to fix: force tombstone flush on demote, or make handoff transfer a compacted tombstone delta.

marco: Flushing every demote could be expensive. But we can make demote ensure at-least the tombstone digest for that prefix is persisted (small metadata) rather than full entries. New owner can then reconcile by pulling entries newer than that digest.

anya: I like digest approach. Minimal IO: old owner writes prefix-tombstone-checkpoint = {epoch, digest, last_seq}. New owner fetches digest and runs quick reconcile: ask for keys in difference window.

emma: Caveat: computing digest cheaply is tricky when compaction has run. We already dedupe tombstones in slab compactor; digest must be consistent snapshot.

ryan: Implementation sketch: on demote: snapshot tombstone bitmap for the prefix -> compute small 64-bit hash + last_seq -> sign into demote_token. New owner uses fast-range scan against retained WAL/immem snapshot on old owner or shared index to backfill any missing tombstones.

marco: That requires the old owner to be able to serve that delta after it's demoted. If it's already shutting down or evicting workers, we need a fallback: new owner can request delta from shared store if present, or mark prefix as "reconcile-needed" and forward reads to sequencer until reconcile completes.

anya: We should avoid long read-forward windows. So plan: attempt in-proc delta pull (short RPC to old owner). If RPC fails or times out (<200ms), fallback to read-forwarding for short TTL and queue full prefill.

emma: Also add telemetry: demote-with-compaction spikes, demote-reconcile-duration, reconcile-fallback-rate. Gate feature behind ff.

ryan: For durability: ensure digest is computed from a persisted snapshot (WAL offset). If digest references only in-memory state, we get the same bug. So pipeline: flush tombstone-snapshot metadata to small checkpoint file or shared index prior to emitting token. That should be cheap (append-only small write).

marco: Tradeoff: additional small writes on demote but only metadata. This is similar to earlier token-with-seq idea but specifically for tombstones/deltas. Should be acceptable.

anya: Also propose an invariant check in debug builds: after handoff, probe a tiny number of tombstoned keys (sample) and alert if any are live on the new owner. Canary will catch correctness regressions quickly.

emma: Edgecase: concurrent compaction and demote could produce races where tombstone was removed and entries reinserted. Add a reconciler that can detect surprising resurrection and emit a corrective tombstone or trigger a more expensive full prefill.

ryan: Operational plan: feature-flag rollout -> canary on low-traffic clusters -> enable digest checkpointing + reconcile path -> monitor reconcile-fallback-rate and read-error-rate -> if > threshold abort.

marco: I'll prototype the digest + small checkpoint writer. anya can own the reconcile RPC and read-path fallback. emma will wire telemetry.

ops-bot: Created task RM-2301: "tombstone-digest-demote-and-reconcile" assigned to marco, anya, emma. :white_check_mark:

anya: Thanks, team. I'll also add a short note to the migration playbook about avoiding compaction windows during live splits.
